Given is an infinite geometric sequence $(a_n)$, defined for every natural number $n \ge 1$, whose ratio q equals its first term and satisfies $|q| < 1$. The ratio of the sum $S_N$ of all terms of this sequence with odd indices to the sum $S_P$ of all terms with even indices equals the difference of these sums, i.e. $\frac{S_N}{S_P} = S_N - S_P$. Compute q.

tasks.summary_en: Triangle in circle $R=1$: $P(x)=(x+1)\sqrt{1-x^2}$. Max $x$ and area (sum, part c)
tasks.statement_en: Consider all acute isosceles triangles ABC (|AC| = |BC|) inscribed in a circle of radius R = 1. Let x denote the distance from the center of the circle to the base AB of the triangle. a) Show that the area P of each of these triangles, as a function of x, is given by the formula $P(x) = (x+1)\sqrt{1-x^2}$. b) Determine the domain of the function P. c) Compute the length x for the triangle among those considered that has the greatest area. Compute this greatest area.
tasks.notes: parts a) and b) are non-numeric (proof, domain interval); sum is of part c)'s two numeric answers: x + P_max
